```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(ReSpectR)
base <- system.file("extdata", package = "ReSpectR")
stopifnot(nzchar(base), dir.exists(base))
```

## Scope: an illustration, not the full validation audit

This vignette runs the updated R workflow and compares its output with
historical Python files bundled in `inst/extdata`. It does not execute Python
and does not establish that these bundled files were generated using the
fixed Python 2.1 revisions and settings of the separate validation audit.
Differences may reflect reference settings or versions as well as numerical
behaviour; the tables below are descriptive, not pass/fail tests.

The documented audit covered 23 configurations, with 20 passing all applicable
recorded numerical criteria and 22 returning identical final mode counts.
See the installed `VALIDATION-2026-10-07.md` record for its scope and limitations.
The 16 examples below do not reproduce that audit or its acceptance thresholds.

The R calculations here explicitly use `solver = "experimental"`, `ns = 100`
and `lamDensity = 2`. Historical frequency examples enable a plateau for
test1u and test7, retaining the bundled example configuration. These settings
are not asserted to match every bundled Python calculation.

## Comparison helpers

H is the natural logarithm of the positive continuous spectrum: h = exp(H).
An additional column in a spectrum output can contain uncertainty information
or a placeholder; it is not the imaginary part of H. Only the first two
columns (relaxation time and log-spectrum) are used here.

Grids are checked numerically rather than assumed identical. For descriptive
comparisons we interpolate the Python log-spectrum against log relaxation time
and Python fitted moduli against log time or log angular frequency. Only R
points within the Python range are compared; no extrapolation is performed.
This interpolation is for reporting and does not change either fitted spectrum.

```{r helpers}
read_reference <- function(domain, test) {
  sub <- if (domain == "time") "py_output_time" else "py_output_freq"
  directory <- file.path(base, sub, test)
  read <- function(name) {
    as.matrix(utils::read.table(file.path(directory, name), comment.char = "#"))
  }
  list(H = read("H.dat"), Gfit = read("Gfit.dat"),
       dmodes = read("dmodes.dat"))
}

on_common_grid <- function(x_r, x_py, y_py) {
  stopifnot(length(x_py) == length(y_py), length(x_py) >= 2L,
            all(is.finite(x_r)), all(x_r > 0),
            all(is.finite(x_py)), all(x_py > 0),
            all(is.finite(y_py)), all(diff(x_py) > 0))
  keep <- x_r >= min(x_py) & x_r <= max(x_py)
  if (!any(keep)) stop("No overlapping grid points.")
  list(keep = keep, reference = stats::approx(
    log(x_py), y_py, xout = log(x_r[keep]), rule = 1
  )$y)
}

compare_case <- function(domain, test, plateau = FALSE) {
  sub <- if (domain == "time") "time_tests" else "freq_tests"
  par <- setParams(
    domain = domain, dataFile = file.path(base, sub, paste0(test, ".dat")),
    solver = "experimental", ns = 100L, lamDensity = 2L,
    plateau = plateau, verbose = FALSE, plotting = FALSE
  )
  crs <- getContinuousSpectrum(par, writeOutput = FALSE)
  drs <- getDiscreteSpectrum(par, crs = crs, writeOutput = FALSE)
  py <- read_reference(domain, test)
  h <- on_common_grid(crs$s, py$H[, 1], py$H[, 2])
  h_difference <- crs$H[h$keep] - h$reference
  n_components <- if (domain == "time") 1L else 2L
  stopifnot(ncol(crs$Gfit) >= n_components + 1L,
            ncol(py$Gfit) >= n_components + 1L)
  differences <- references <- numeric()
  n_common <- integer(n_components)
  for (j in seq_len(n_components)) {
    z <- on_common_grid(crs$Gfit[, 1], py$Gfit[, 1], py$Gfit[, j + 1L])
    differences <- c(differences, crs$Gfit[z$keep, j + 1L] - z$reference)
    references <- c(references, z$reference)
    n_common[j] <- sum(z$keep)
  }
  stopifnot(all(is.finite(h_difference)), all(is.finite(differences)))
  relative_rms <- if (all(references != 0)) {
    sqrt(mean((differences / references)^2))
  } else NA_real_
  same_h_grid <- length(crs$s) == nrow(py$H) &&
    isTRUE(all.equal(as.numeric(crs$s), as.numeric(py$H[, 1]),
                     tolerance = 1e-5, check.attributes = FALSE))
  data.frame(
    domain = domain, test = test, plateau = plateau,
    N_nominal_R = drs$Nopt, N_final_R = length(drs$tau),
    N_final_Python_file = nrow(py$dmodes),
    H_grid_agrees_at_tolerance = same_h_grid,
    H_points_compared = sum(h$keep), H_points_R = length(crs$s),
    H_RMSE = sqrt(mean(h_difference^2)),
    curve_points_per_component = min(n_common),
    curve_points_R = nrow(crs$Gfit),
    curve_RMSE = sqrt(mean(differences^2)),
    curve_relative_RMS_to_Python_fit = relative_rms
  )
}
```

## Time-domain examples

```{r time-comparison}
time_results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(paste0("test", 1:7), function(test) {
  compare_case("time", test, plateau = FALSE)
}))
knitr::kable(time_results, digits = 6)
```

## Frequency-domain examples

```{r frequency-comparison}
frequency_tests <- c("test1", "test1n", "test1u", paste0("test", 2:7))
frequency_results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(frequency_tests, function(test) {
  compare_case("frequency", test, plateau = test %in% c("test1u", "test7"))
}))
knitr::kable(frequency_results, digits = 6)
```

## How to interpret these tables

- `N_nominal_R` is the AIC-selected nominal mode count; `N_final_R` counts
  surviving relaxation times after refinement, pruning and merging.
- `N_final_Python_file` counts rows in the bundled `dmodes.dat`. It does not
  recover Python's nominal AIC-selected count. A count difference is not
  automatically harmless and requires investigation under matched settings.
- H errors are on the log-spectrum scale and are computed only on the
  overlapping range. The reported point counts expose excluded points.
- Curve RMSE pools the time-domain modulus or both frequency-domain moduli.
  Relative RMS is normalised by the interpolated Python fitted values, not
  by experimental observations. It is NA if a reference value is zero.
- Agreement of two reconstructions does not show that either fits the
  observations well. In particular, a positive relaxation-spectrum model
  constrains the storage modulus to be non-decreasing with frequency, even
  when a constant equilibrium modulus is included.
- These examples do not compare uncertainty estimates, merge counts or every
  intermediate control in the separate audit. They do not certify numerical
  equivalence or identify a unique physical spectrum.

For a reproducible cross-implementation claim, retain the source revisions,
input data, complete settings, comparison thresholds and detailed results.
